x: Pritchard running a fine third leg, we had the satisfaction of beating Mitcham A.C., with Epsom beating Croydon for third place. The 4 x 880 yards saw Dick Michael give us the lead on the first stage, but F.
Beer, who is only just out of the junior stage, but who shows steady improvement; while F.
Arthur Beaumont, Fred White, Dick Michael, Ted Stimpson, Percy Wright, Alby Bird, Joe Daly and George Murray are also frequent strollers, and now the prodigal Alf Taylor has returned to the fold.

Stride, Jnr., a very promising young runner with a fine stride (excuse the pun!) and he made good use of his start to run home an easy winner. Freddy White showed that marathons had not taken all his pace and ran well to gain second place; with a newcomer in R.

Freddy White went next and, running in fine style, he easily overhauled his man and took us into the lead. Syd Jarlett strode round to keep our advantage and sent Alby Bird off with a winning margin, which the Mitcham man did not attempt to cut down.
Mitchell ran well to gain first class standards; and Bert Lindsey and F.

Dick Michael led the others at the last bend and looked as though he would be runner-up, but Sid Jarlett had other ideas, fought him down the straight, and just “pipped” him. Standards (2 min. 8 sec.) were gained by F.
Bowers was also 2nd in the 220 yards, with Jarlett 3rd. Marchant won the 440 yards, and F.

Fred White, who was making his last appearance for the Club owing to his being called for the R.A.F., finished 2nd. The field events men—Syd Jones and Bill Sutton—gained full points in most of the field events.
Freddy White.—News has reached us that Freddy is now married and a Corporal. Stationed somewhere in the Thames Valley, he won six firsts for his R.A.F.
Morris, the Indoor Champion in a ding-dong finish, with Freddy White taking third place for the South. The 1 Mile was won by Pascoe, of North London.

Allen (N.F.S.), the old Highgate International had the measure of the field in the mile which was perhaps the best race of the afternoon, with Hines 2nd, Forde 3rd and Freddy White 4th, in the excellent time of 4.36.

Fred White, is another who has started training again, and hopes to be running in the Marathon this year.

Thorne, who was next home for the Club also ran very well indeed, seeing that this was his first appearance this season, he finished 11th, so it is obvious that if he were to train regularly he would go near winning. F.
